chief_complaint: Hypertension management with early chronic kidney disease and diabetic kidney involvement
history_of_present_illness: 53-year-old white male with essential hypertension since 1995 on lisinopril and amlodipine. Blood pressure remains elevated diastolic (122/92 mmHg). Chronic kidney disease stage 2 diagnosed 2016 with micro‑albuminuria attributed to type 2 diabetes mellitus (diagnosed 2016). Chronic kidney disease stage 1 and diabetic kidney disease have been present since 2012. Chronic pain, low back pain, and neck pain are managed with acetaminophen. Social isolation, limited social contact, part‑time employment, and a criminal record are documented. No antidiabetic therapy or recent labs (A1c, eGFR, lipids, BMI) are available. Last encounter documented March 2017.

active_problems.name: Microalbuminuria due to type 2 diabetes mellitus
Disorder of kidney due to diabetes mellitus

past_medical_history: History of appendectomy (1976). Resolved gingivitis (2016–2017). Resolved stress (2016–2017). Prior full‑time employment (resolved 2017). No other chronic conditions documented.

active_medications.name: Lisinopril 10 mg oral tablet
active_medications.purpose: Blood pressure control and renal protection (hypertension, CKD)

risk_factor_summary: CARDIOVASCULAR: Elevated risk for ischemic heart disease, heart failure, stroke, and peripheral vascular disease due to longstanding hypertension, diabetes‑related kidney disease, CKD, age >50 (male), and likely dyslipidemia (no statin documented). RENAL: High risk for CKD progression to ESRD given hypertension, diabetes, micro‑albuminuria, and CKD stage 2; ACE‑I therapy present but recent eGFR and urine studies missing. METABOLIC: Diabetes mellitus is present (micro‑albuminuria) but no antidiabetic medication or recent A1c; risk for worsening hyperglycemia. HEMATOLOGIC: Potential anemia of chronic disease/CKD (CBC not available). NEUROLOGIC: Increased stroke risk from vascular comorbidities; no cognitive decline documented.

data_quality_flags.issue: Missing recent estimated glomerular filtration rate

clinical_impression: Patient has uncontrolled diastolic hypertension, stage 2 CKD secondary to type 2 diabetes‑related kidney disease, and multiple chronic pain conditions. Social factors (isolation, limited contact, part‑time work, criminal record) add to overall risk. The combination places him at high risk for cardiovascular events, renal function decline, and diabetes progression, and the lack of recent laboratory monitoring limits optimal management.
